$(B(t), 0 \le t < \infty)$ is standard Brownian motion (BM),

Consider $M(t) = \max_{0 \le s \le t} B(s)$. The joint density of $(M(t), B(t))$ is

$$f_{M(t),B(t)}(a, b) = \frac{2(2a - b)}{\sqrt{2\pi}} t^{-3/2} \exp(-(2a - b)^2/(2t)); \quad a \ge 0,\ a \ge b.$$

This formula is complicated, but there are two interesting consequences.

### Proposition

$$\mathbb{P}(M_1 > a \mid B(1) = 0) = \exp(-2a^2), \quad a > 0.$$

$$\mathbb{P}(B(1) \le -b \mid M(1) = 0) = \exp(-b^2/2), \quad b > 0.$$

---

Other calculations we can do involve

$$L = \sup\{t \le 1 : B(t) = 0\}; \quad R = \inf\{t \ge 1 : B(t) = 0\}.$$

(Jargon: the **excursion** containing time 1 happens over the interval $[L, R]$.) The results are

$$f_R(t) = \frac{1}{\pi(t - 1)^{1/2} t}, \quad 1 < t < \infty$$

$$\mathbb{P}(L \le s) = 2\pi^{-1} \arcsin s^{1/2}, \quad 0 < s < 1. \tag{1}$$

$$f_L(s) = \frac{1}{\pi s^{1/2}(1 - s)^{1/2}}, \quad 0 < s < 1 \quad \text{(arcsine distribution)}.$$

On the board I will show

$$\mathbb{P}(L \le s) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty g_s(x) \phi_s(x)\, dx$$

$$g_s(x) = \mathbb{P}(T_{|x|} > 1 - s) = 1 - 2\bar{\Phi}(|x|/\sqrt{1 - s}), \quad \phi_s(\cdot) \text{ is density of } B(s).$$

Then (1) is a hard calculus exercise!
